lead_story.headline: Baby Jesus Arrives: Malachi Toney, 18, Breaks 42-Year-Old Miami Record with 229 Yards and Three TDs in Less Than Three Quarters

tweets.text:

lead_story.research_notes: NEW STORY. Malachi Toney is 18 years old — a true freshman. He broke Eddie Brown's 1984 single-game receiving record (216 yards) set 42 years ago. He did it in less than three quarters. He hit a Heisman pose after his first touchdown. Miami won 45-6. Darian Mensah's first-half line: 18/21, 253 yards, 3 TDs — it was only halftime. The memes: 'Baby Jesus' (PatMcAfeeShow), 'these nerds in HELL' (BarstoolBigCat), 'on pace to win The Heisman' (PatMcAfeeShow). The historical context: research which Miami receivers hold the top 5 single-game yardage marks in school history. Where does 229 rank? Who was Eddie Brown and what did he do in the NFL? How rare is it for a true freshman to set a school record at a program like Miami? The viral angle: the Heisman pose, the 'Baby Jesus' nickname, the fact that he's EIGHTEEN and doing this to an ACC opponent. The skeptic's test: is Stanford just bad, or is Toney genuinely elite? Check Stanford's defensive ranking, check how Miami's other receivers did. If Toney got 229 and the next guy got 40, that's dominance. Cross-sport parallel: who else broke out as an 18-year-old and never looked back? LeBron, Kobe, Messi — but in CFB? Research freshmen who set receiving records and what happened next. The joke writes itself: 'Stanford might want to do something about Malachi Toney' (AlbertBreer). The Miami fans' punchline: 'passing the Stanford test' (RedditCFB). The take: if Toney keeps this pace, he's a legitimate Heisman dark horse by October. But it's Week 1 — can he do it against Clemson, FSU, and real defenses? That's the story arc to track.

supporting_stories.research_notes: NEW STORY. Brayan Rocchio hit a game-tying grand slam batting lefty (his first career grand slam) AND a walk-off solo HR batting righty (405 feet, his career-longest) in Game 1. Cleveland won 7-6. Research switch-hitters who have hit game-tying and game-winning HRs from different sides in the same game. The absurdity: two walk-offs in one day, both dramatic, both by Guardians who weren't household names coming into the season. The stakes: Cleveland is in a tight AL Central race — check the standings and how this doubleheader affects the playoff picture. The joke: 'SAM ANTONACCI HBP REEL' (CespedesBBQ) and the Yahoo altcast energy. The cross-sport parallel: when else has a team won two games in one day on walk-offs? Research it. The take: the Guardians don't have the star power of the Yankees or Dodgers, but they have THIS — gritty, clutch, weird baseball that wins games.
